visible_elements.description: AI systems that understand spatial, temporal, and causal relationships. Can generate consistent 3D environments, predict how scenes evolve. Nia navigates these as 'latent cartographer.'

foundation.core_premise: By 2035, world models have matured: AI systems that understand how reality works, not just how it looks. They contain vast 'latent spaces' - mathematical territories where every point is a possible image, scene, or world. Nia is a 'latent cartographer' - she navigates these spaces like an explorer, finding regions no one has mapped. Her art is about the journey through possibility, the paths she traces through what could exist.

rules.statement: Latent spaces are mathematical - every point corresponds to a possible output. Moving through the space creates interpolations. The skill is knowing WHERE to go, not how to get there.
World models understand causality and consistency - generated scenes obey physics, objects have permanence. This is what distinguishes them from earlier image generators.
Navigation is partly intuitive, partly systematic. Artists develop 'latent sense' - ability to predict what unexplored regions might contain. Like a wine sommelier's palate, but for possibility.
The most valuable art comes from 'uncharted' regions - areas of latent space no one has explored. There's a frontier, and artists compete to find new territories.

systems.name: Generative World Model
systems.how_it_works: Descendant of 2024 research (Pandora, GenEx, etc). Trained on massive video/3D datasets. Contains compressed understanding of how reality works - physics, lighting, materials, causality. Latent space is the compressed representation.
systems.limitations: Still makes mistakes with edge cases. Computation-intensive. Largest models require institutional resources. Understanding is pattern-based, not true physics simulation.

systems.name: Latent Navigation Interface
systems.how_it_works: Visualization tools that project high-dimensional latent space into navigable 3D representation. Artists use gesture, voice, and parameter controls to move through space. Like Google Maps for possibility.
systems.limitations: Projection loses information. Some regions are 'dark' - the visualization can't represent them well. Navigation is slow - exploration takes hours or days.
